hypotheses.justification: The statement only mentions `S : OpenNormalSubgroup G`, `x : finiteTateNegOne A L S` and `finiteTateNegOneι A L S x`, all of which are built from material that never takes `IsTopologicalGroup G`. `LevelCompact` (LevelCompact.lean, `structure LevelCompact (A : Rep.{uA} R G)`, line 93) is defined in a context with only `[CommRing R] [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]`, and `finiteCoinvariants`, `group` and `normFromFiniteCoinvariants` are stated and proved in `FiniteCoinvariants.lean` (lines 247, 481, 521) in a section whose only variables are `[CommRing R]`, `[Group G]`, `[TopologicalSpace G]`; `CompHausAddCommGrp.kernelGroup` and `kernelι` (CompactAddCommGroup.lean, lines 154 and 174) are generic in the category. Since `finiteTateNegOne` and `finiteTateNegOneι` are an `abbrev` and a `def` (not theorems), Lean computes their argument lists from header + value, so these instances are not even arguments of them; consequently the modified statement elaborates unchanged in the restricted context (`omit [IsTopologicalGroup G] in ...`) and `rfl` still closes the goal. This is exactly the pattern already used in the same file, e.g. `omit [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] in` at lines 120 and 172.

Same argument: nothing in the statement needs compactness of `G`. `LevelCompact A` carries its own per-level compactness data (`L.compact`), and `finiteCoinvariants`/`normFromFiniteCoinvariants`/`group` are defined and reasoned about in `FiniteCoinvariants.lean` without any `CompactSpace G` hypothesis in scope (section variables at line 232 are only `[Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]`), while `CompHausAddCommGrp.kernelGroup`/`kernelι` are generic. So deleting `[CompactSpace G]` (via `omit [CompactSpace G] in`, or together with `[IsTopologicalGroup G]` as at lines 120/172 of the same file) leaves the elaboration of `finiteTateNegOne A L S`, `finiteTateNegOneι A L S` and of the conclusion intact, and the proof is still `rfl`. The two omissions are independent and may be made simultaneously.
